OpsBot: Paging: SLO alert triggered for continuous-batching path in us-west2 — p95 and p99 spikes for streaming endpoints > 30s. Incident created: <https://redwood.incidents/INC-174650|INC-174650> :rotating_light:

Alex (oncall): saw the page, jumping in. basic telemetry? which cluster?

Maya (sre): looks like us-west2-pool-3. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 12s, p99 to ~38s starting 12:30 UTC. correlates with elevated mix of long seqs. CPU on batcher pods ~85%, GPU utilization normal.

Jon (eng-runtime): interesting — continuous-batching scheduler backlog spiked. logs show a small number of huge sequences (30k tokens?) blocking pack windows. here's a sample from the batcher log: 

```
2026-03-14T12:30:41Z batcher[pack_scheduler] INFO pack_window: 150 reqs, max_seq=29120, avg_seq=384
2026-03-14T12:30:41Z batcher[pack_scheduler] WARN hold_time=11234ms, tail_wait=28912ms
2026-03-14T12:30:42Z runtime[streamer] ERROR stall_detected session=xxx latency=31012ms
```

Alex (oncall): so mixed-seqlen pathological packs holding streaming lanes. customer impact?

Rita (cs): two customers opened support cases around 12:40 UTC complaining about timeouts on streaming endpoints. both are mid-enterprise PLG clients. I can draft a short note if we need customer-facing comms.

Jon (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations I can flip (low-risk):
- enable `pack_shed=true` for us-west2-pool-3 to avoid oversized packs
- reduce `pack_window_ms` from 50 -> 20 for streaming route
- temporarily set `stream_priority=high` for streaming workers

Maya (sre): +1 to those. also we should evict long running KV entries that keep cache pinned. I can run an eviction script on affected nodes.

Alex (oncall): do it. Jon, can you push pack_shed and window change now? include a canary on 2 nodes first.

Jon (eng-runtime): doing canary on pool-3/node-7 -> applying config now.

OpsBot: Config change applied on pool-3/node-7 by Jon at 12:46 UTC. Monitoring for 5m.

Maya (sre): running KV eviction on pool-3 nodes 7-9 now. command: `./kv_evict --nodes pool-3 --age 120m --dry-run=false`

Alex (oncall): early telemetry?

Jon (eng-runtime): canary shows p95 dropped to ~280ms, p99 to ~1.2s on node-7 streaming route. good sign. rolling to remaining nodes in 2 batches.

Maya (sre): KV eviction finished. freed ~4.2GB of KV cache on each node. tail stalls reduced in logs.

PagerDuty Bot: Acknowledge from oncall: Alex. Escalation to eng-runtime: Jon.

Alex (oncall): rolling changes now. Jon, coordinate throttle so we don't thrash packer.

Jon (eng-runtime): rolling config to remaining nodes. sequence: node-8,node-9 then rest. will pause 90s between nodes.

Rita (cs): customer impact update: both customers see requests succeed again after 12:55 UTC. reaching out to confirm no data loss and ask for timeline. prepping a short blurb: "We experienced elevated streaming latency due to a batching scheduler issue; mitigation applied and performance restored. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

Alex (oncall): good. postmortem owners? Jon + Maya to triage root cause. I'll keep incident open for 2-3 hours for monitoring.

Jon (eng-runtime): initial root cause hypothesis: scheduler uses max_seq in pack decision causing single huge seq to expand batch hold_time. long-term fix options:
- change packer bias: cap per-request seq contribution or max_pack_seq threshold
- implement per-sequence timeout for batch formation to prevent indefinite hold
- prioritize streaming requests via separate fast-path that disallows packing with >X token requests

Maya (sre): also add alert for pack_hold_time > 5s and a synthetic that sends mixed-seqlen traffic to catch regressions.

Alex (oncall): action items summarized: 
- Jon: rollout config toggle and implement pack_shed short-term, own runtime changes for packer (ETA 3d)
- Maya: KV eviction script permanent runbook + alert tuning (ETA 1d)
- Rita: customer comms sent and follow-up scheduled (ETA 1h)
- Alex: draft incident summary and keep monitoring open (ETA 2h)

Rita (cs): sent initial customer messages at 13:05 UTC. will update thread with replies.

OpsBot: Incident INC-174650 updated: status=mitigated, severity=SEV2, oncall=Alex.

Alex (oncall): closing handoff. leaving notes for postmortem. if latency resurfaces, re-open page. thanks everyone :heart:

Jon (eng-runtime): saving logs + traces to the incident ticket and labelling `contbatch-mixedlen`. will follow up with proposed PR for packer change.

Maya (sre): monitoring looks stable for 20m. p95/p99 back within SLO. marking as monitored.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident closed by Alex at 13:25 UTC (auto-close window).
